question.problem: Calculate the integral $\displaystyle{\int} (2\sec^2 x + \sec x \tan x )\, \textrm{d}x.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
\int \sec^2 x \, \textrm dx = \tan x + C
$$

and

$$
\int \sec x \tan x \, \textrm dx = \sec x + C.
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\eqalign{
		\int (2\sec^2 x + \sec x \tan x )\, \textrm{d}x& = 2 \int \sec^2 x \, \textrm{d}x+ \int \sec x \tan x \, \textrm{d}x \
										&=2\tan x + \sec x + C.

}
$$
